rows.grounds: relative pronoun referring to purifying persons

items.question: Who besides those whose contact purifies others deserves worship?
premises: Some persons purify others by their contact.
Such purifying persons are supremely worthy of honor.
No other candidate surpasses their purifying power.
items.inference: Therefore none other than those purifying persons should be worshipped.
items.plain_english: Who else should be worshipped besides those by whose mere contact others are purified?

rows.grounds: upon the surface of the earth

items.question: What status do those gain who worship the purifying ones even once with devotion?
premises: Some people worship the purifying ones even once.
That worship is performed with devotion.
Devotional worship confers worthiness of honor.
items.inference: Therefore even such worshippers become worthy of worship on earth.
items.plain_english: Those who worship them even once with devotion are themselves worthy of worship on earth.

items.question: Can even an outcaste attain the Kaula state through proper refuge?
premises: An outcaste may take refuge in a qualified person.
Such refuge can bring purification.
Purification enables attainment of the Kaula state.
items.inference: Therefore even an outcaste, having taken refuge and become purified, may attain the Kaula state.
items.plain_english: Even an outcaste who, having taken refuge in such a one, becomes purified may attain the Kaula state.

items.question: How do all other dharmas relate to the encompassing Kula dharma?
premises: Kula dharma is presented as a comprehensive path.
All other dharmas are compared to things immersed in it.
Immersion implies inclusion within a greater whole.
items.inference: Therefore all dharmas are immersed in Kula dharma.
items.plain_english: O beloved, all dharmas are thus immersed in the Kula dharma.

items.question: Whom can the purifying practitioners elevate through their association?
premises: Certain practitioners possess purifying power.
Their associates include mlecchas, śvapacas, and lowly people.
Purifying power extends to those associates.
items.inference: Therefore these practitioners purify even their mleccha, śvapaca, and lowly associates.
items.plain_english: They purify their own associates, even mlecchas, śvapacas, and other lowly people.

items.question: What transformation occurs for all who enter into Kula conduct?
premises: People may enter into Kula conduct.
Kula conduct confers Kaula identity.
This applies inclusively to all who enter.
items.inference: Therefore all who enter Kula conduct attain the Kaula state.
items.plain_english: Even all who enter into Kula conduct attain the state of being Kaula.

items.question: Do people remain distinct after immersion in the ocean of Kula?
premises: People may become immersed in the ocean of Kula.
Immersion implies merging into a single whole.
Merged elements do not remain separate.
items.inference: Therefore people immersed in the Kula ocean would not remain separate.
items.plain_english: Thus, people immersed in the ocean of Kula would not remain separate.

items.question: Who becomes qualified to participate in this Kula conduct?
premises: Immersion in Kula removes prior separateness.
Kula conduct requires qualification.
Those merged in Kula gain that qualification.
items.inference: Therefore all of them would become qualified in this Kula conduct.
items.plain_english: All of them would become qualified in this Kula conduct.

rows.grounds: a specific social or occupational group

items.question: Which diverse groups are included among those considered in this context?
premises: The text enumerates specific social groups.
Actors, karaṇas, khasas, and drāviḍas are named.
The enumeration indicates inclusivity of diverse groups.
items.inference: Therefore actors, karaṇas, khasas, and drāviḍas are included among those considered.
uncertainties: Exact social referents of karaṇaḥ and khasaḥ in this context are traditional group names.
items.plain_english: Actors, karaṇas, khasas, and drāviḍas are among those included.

items.question: What fate befalls those who have fallen away from all dharmas?
premises: Some persons are fallen from all dharmas.
Loss of dharma leads to degraded outcomes.
The text states their resulting destination.
items.inference: Therefore those fallen from all dharmas go to the lowest state.
items.plain_english: Fallen from all dharmas, they go to the lowest state.

items.question: What consequence awaits a Kaula who deceives those fallen from dharma?
premises: A Kaula may deceive those who are fallen.
Deceiving the vulnerable is a grave transgression.
Grave transgression leads to hellish punishment.
items.inference: Therefore even a Kaula who deceives them would go to the Raurava hell.
items.plain_english: Even a Kaula who deceives them would go to the hell called Raurava.

items.question: What becomes of a Kaula who fails to perform the Kaula rite?
premises: A Kaula is expected to perform the Kaula rite.
Failure to perform it contradicts Kaula duty.
Such failure results in a degraded destination.
items.inference: Therefore a Kaula who does not perform the Kaula rite goes to a downward state.
items.plain_english: A Kaula who does not perform the Kaula rite is the lowest and goes to a downward state.

items.question: How much merit arises from performing a rite for a single Kaula?
premises: Service to a Kaula is highly valued.
The text quantifies the resulting merit.
The merit is vastly multiplied.
items.inference: Therefore merit ten million times greater arises when it is done for one Kaula.
items.plain_english: Therefore, when it is done for even one Kaula, the merit is ten million times greater.

items.question: What ultimate attainment follows for those who become Kaulas and are freed from bonds?
premises: Some become Kaulas.
Kaula realization brings freedom from bonds.
Freedom from bonds leads to the supreme goal.
items.inference: Therefore they become Kaulas, are freed from bonds, and go to the supreme state.
items.plain_english: They become Kaulas, freed from bonds, and go to the supreme state.

items.question: How should Kaula practitioners relate to one another in mutual conduct?
premises: Kaula practitioners are to be worshipped and honored.
Affection, faith, and love are prescribed attitudes.
These attitudes are to be mutual.
items.inference: Therefore they should worship and honor one another with affection, faith, and love.
items.plain_english: They should worship and honor one another with affection, faith, and love.

items.question: What serves as the unique bridge for crossing the ocean of worldly existence?
premises: Worldly existence is likened to an ocean to be crossed.
A bridge is needed for crossing it.
Kula dharma is identified as that bridge with no other equal.
items.inference: Therefore Kula dharma alone is the bridge for crossing the ocean of existence.
items.plain_english: Indeed, Kula dharma is the bridge for crossing the ocean of existence, and there is no other.

items.question: How are the entangling nets of karma destroyed through spiritual practice?
premises: Karma forms binding nets.
Kula dharma can be practiced devotedly.
Such practice has the power to destroy karmic nets.
items.inference: Therefore the nets of karma are burned away by the practice of Kula dharma.
items.plain_english: The nets of karma are burned away by the practice of Kula dharma.

items.question: Who should be recognized as the foremost among Kaula practitioners?
premises: Some practitioners purify others through Kula conduct.
Purifying others is a mark of excellence.
Such excellence defines the best among Kaulas.
items.inference: Therefore those who purify others by Kula conduct should be known as the best of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: Those who purify others through Kula conduct should be known as the best among Kaulas.

items.question: What purifying function is attributed to the first half of the Mahānirvāṇa Tantra?
premises: The Mahānirvāṇa Tantra has a first half.
This portion is described as purifying the world.
Such description attributes a salvific function to it.
items.inference: Therefore the first half of the Mahānirvāṇa Tantra is world-purifying.
items.plain_english: The first half of the Mahānirvāṇa Tantra is purifying for the world.

items.question: What final attainment awaits one who becomes freed from all sins?
premises: A person may become freed from all sins.
Freedom from sin prepares one for final release.
The text states the ultimate attainment.
items.inference: Therefore one freed from all sins obtains liberation in the end.
items.plain_english: Freed from all sins, he obtains liberation in the end.

items.question: What comprehensive knowledge results from knowing this king of tantras?
premises: This text is called the king of tantras.
Knowing it imparts deep understanding.
That understanding encompasses all scriptures.
items.inference: Therefore one who knows this king of tantras becomes a knower of all scriptures.
items.plain_english: Having known this king of tantras, one becomes a knower of all scriptures.

items.question: What liberation is gained by knowing this great tantra?
premises: This is a great tantra.
Knowing it has liberating power.
Karmic bonds are what bind beings.
items.inference: Therefore one who knows this great tantra is liberated from the bonds of karma.
items.plain_english: One who knows this great tantra is liberated from the bonds of karma.

items.question: What spiritual stature belongs to one who truly knows this teaching?
premises: Knowing this teaching is a profound attainment.
Such knowledge defines a true knower.
The knower is identified as virtuous and a knower of brahman.
items.inference: Therefore one who knows this, O Kālikā, is a knower, a knower of brahman, and virtuous.
items.plain_english: O Kālikā, he who knows this is a knower, a knower of Brahman, and virtuous.

items.question: Why is knowledge of this tantra sufficient compared to studying many other tantras?
premises: Many other tantras exist.
Knowing this tantra confers comprehensive knowledge.
Comprehensive knowledge makes other study unnecessary.
items.inference: Therefore, having known this, one would become all-knowing, so what need is there of many other tantras?
items.plain_english: What need is there of many other tantras? Having known this one, one would become all-knowing.
